messages.content:
The record:
Write the postmortem for the incident below.

Alert: HighErrorRate on io-shop
What the alert said [AL1]: Error rate above threshold for 5m {A1}
Alert raised: 2026-11-14T11:46:29Z {alert_raised}
Nobody was paged: no on-call incident was linked to this one. An alert rule fires; a person is paged. Argus first posted about the incident in Slack at 2026-11-14T11:46:55Z {first_told}, and the document says so already: leave that post out, and do not say that no person was told. That nobody was paged is a finding of its own.
The alert rule waits 5 minutes {rule_waits} with its condition holding before it fires. The alert came within the 7 minutes 30 seconds {accounted_for} accounted for by its rule waiting 5 minutes {rule_waits} with its condition holding, its evaluation at intervals of 1 minute {rule_evaluated_every}, an unmeasured allowance of 30 seconds {scraping_allowance} for scraping and storing its samples and the whole minute the onset is measured to.
Broken from 2026-11-14T11:40:00Z {began} (the onset, dated to its minute: a change came during that minute) to 2026-11-14T11:48:01Z {back_to_normal}, when demo user reported it resolved [XW1] - their report is the end, as given. A report is not a hypothesis: do not test it against the rest of the record, and do not propose checking reports like it. Argus stopping at the report before it judged an action is the design: do not say it went wrong.
That is 8 minutes 1 second {duration}, and every impact figure below is measured over that stretch.
Argus held the incident for 1 minute 11 seconds {held}, until 2026-11-14T11:48:01Z {argus_stopped}. That is not how long the fault lasted, nor how long Argus went on working - leave it out of your answer.
The service's error rate over all its requests, before it began: 0.9% {errors_before}.
The same rate while it was broken: 27.2% {errors_while_broken}, peaking at 40.5% {errors_at_worst}.
Rise above baseline: 26.3% {errors_rise} of traffic failed that otherwise would not have.
The series behind the alert, `sum(rate(http_requests_total{code=~"5.."}[1m])) / sum(rate(http_requests_total[1m]))` - its alert said "Error rate above threshold for 5m {A1}" - which its alert rule evaluates and calls worse rising: 0.9416666666666667% {series_before} before it began, 27.222222222222225% {series_while_broken} on average while it was broken, and 40.5% {series_at_worst} at its worst. Say what it measures in words, not by its query.
Customer loss: 5,422.30 USD {customer_loss} - how far the shop's takings over the incident fell short of the same hours whole weeks earlier, beyond how much those hours vary on their own.

What Argus did, in order:
  - [T1] 2026-11-14T11:46:50Z {T1.1} Argus: Received HighErrorRate on io-shop
  - [T2] 2026-11-14T11:47:02Z {T2.1} Argus: Moved the incident to INVESTIGATING - a worker took the incident up
  - [T3] 2026-11-14T11:47:02Z {T3.1} Argus: Called in the Investigator Agent
  - [T4] 2026-11-14T11:47:11Z {T4.1} Investigator Agent: Asked for the service's per-minute metrics, anchored on 11:46:29 {T4.2}
  - [T5] 2026-11-14T11:47:18Z {T5.1} Investigator Agent: Read back 361 {T5.2} minutes of metrics
  - [T6] 2026-11-14T11:47:20Z {T6.1} Investigator Agent: Placed the start of the incident at 11:40 {T6.2}
  - [T7] 2026-11-14T11:47:20Z {T7.1} Investigator Agent: Recorded where the 3 {T7.2} replicas run - all on Tesla-V100-SXM2-16GB
  - [T8] 2026-11-14T11:47:22Z {T8.1} Investigator Agent: Asked for production change events - deploys and releases, and flag changes from the flag provider's history, the 1 {T8.2} day 1 {T8.3} minute before Nov 14 11:41 {T8.4}
  - [T9] 2026-11-14T11:47:23Z {T9.1} Investigator Agent: Read back 1 {T9.2} production change
  - [T10] 2026-11-14T11:47:24Z {T10.1} Investigator Agent: Read how far the deployment had rolled out - all 3 {T10.2} replicas run one revision, which the history does not name
  - [T11] 2026-11-14T11:47:24Z {T11.1} Investigator Agent: Asked for the service's log lines, the 36 {T11.2} minutes 29 {T11.3} seconds before 11:46:29 {T11.4}
  - [T12] 2026-11-14T11:47:24Z {T12.1} Investigator Agent: Read back 124 {T12.2} log lines
  - [T13] 2026-11-14T11:47:27Z {T13.1} Investigator Agent: Formed 1 {T13.2} candidate cause, best first: C1
  - [T14] 2026-11-14T11:47:27Z {T14.1} Investigator Agent: Read every channel available
  - [T15] 2026-11-14T11:47:27Z {T15.1} Argus: Read the flag provider's history - 1 {T15.2} flag change by anyone but Argus, the 1 {T15.3} hour before 11:47:27 {T15.4}
  - [T16] 2026-11-14T11:47:32Z {T16.1} Argus: Moved the incident to MITIGATING to act on a candidate
  - [T17] 2026-11-14T11:47:33Z {T17.1} Argus: Called in the Mitigation Agent
  - [T18] 2026-11-14T11:47:36Z {T18.1} Mitigation Agent: Reverted the feature flag monthly-spend-feature for C1, moved from ON to OFF
  - [T19] 2026-11-14T11:47:46Z {T19.1} Mitigation Agent: Waiting to see whether the service is still at the incident's level, from 11:48 {T19.2} - up to 143s {T19.3}
  - [T20] 2026-11-14T11:47:46Z {T20.1} Mitigation Agent: Looked at the service - no new minute read yet
  - [XW1] 2026-11-14T11:48:01Z {XW1.1} demo user: Moved the incident to RESOLVED from the Argus UI - kept the flag off and told the checkout team
  - [T21] 2026-11-14T11:48:02Z {T21.1} Mitigation Agent: Stopped before judging the action - a person ended the incident

Changes to production it read:
  - [P1] 2026-11-14T11:40:31Z {P1.1} flag-toggle monthly-spend-feature by admin: feature flag monthly-spend-feature was switched on
  - Deploys read, none came back.

Log lines it read, one per message:
  - [G7e5d] INFO io-shop: monthly-spend-feature=off - 200 {G7e5d.1} evaluations - 30 {G7e5d.2} occurrences in 30 {G7e5d.3} minutes, 11:10–11:39 {G7e5d.4}
  - [G46bc] ERROR io-shop: account page request failed - ClientDisconnected: the shopper closed the connection - 36 {G46bc.1} occurrences in 30 {G46bc.2} minutes, 11:10–11:39 {G46bc.3}
  - [Gbac1] WARN io-shop: account page error rate at #% over the last minute - 27 {Gbac1.1} occurrences in 37 {Gbac1.2} minutes, 11:10–11:46 {Gbac1.3}; # was 0.50% {Gbac1.4} to 40.50% {Gbac1.5}, typically 1.50% {Gbac1.6}, highest at 11:43 {Gbac1.7}
  - [Gad41] INFO io-shop: account pages rendered normally - 10 {Gad41.1} occurrences in 26 {Gad41.2} minutes, 11:11–11:36 {Gad41.3}
  - [G971b] INFO io-shop: monthly-spend-feature=off 101 {G971b.1} / on 99 {G971b.2} - 200 {G971b.3} evaluations - 1 {G971b.4} occurrence in 1 {G971b.5} minute, 11:40 {G971b.6}
  - [G5309] ERROR io-shop: account page request failed - ZeroDivisionError: division by zero at src/io_shop/spend_summary.py:47 - 14 {G5309.1} occurrences in 7 {G5309.2} minutes, 11:40–11:46 {G5309.3}
  - [Gce95] INFO io-shop: monthly-spend-feature=on - 200 {Gce95.1} evaluations - 6 {Gce95.2} occurrences in 6 {Gce95.3} minutes, 11:41–11:46 {Gce95.4}

Candidates it considered, in the Investigator's words - name them by their labels, but cite none; what they claim is not what happened unless a row of the record shows it:
  - [C1] The feature flag monthly-spend-feature was switched from off to on at 2026-11-14T11:40:31Z {C1.1}. The newly enabled spend-summary path then raised ZeroDivisionError at src/io_shop/spend_summary.py:47 on account page requests, and the error rate rose from about 1% {C1.2} to 20-40% {C1.3}. [feature-flag-toggle, confidence 0.93 {C1.4}, tried, not judged]

Actions it took:
  - [M1] Reverted the feature flag monthly-spend-feature for [C1] (can be put back) - not judged, still in place

Action items the record already holds:
  - none
The document already states what set it off, in a section of its own: the change [P1] - suspected, not confirmed.

Cite evidence in causal_chain by its label. In a contributing factor's addressed_by, name the record's own action items that answer it, by their number; an item you propose names the factors it answers in its answers, by their labels.

Call submit_postmortem with your answer.

The document, by field:
root_cause: Switching monthly-spend-feature on sent account page requests through the spend-summary code, which divided by zero at src/io_shop/spend_summary.py:47 and failed the request with a ZeroDivisionError. The record does not show why the divisor was zero on these requests.
cause_in_plain_words: Turning on a new monthly-spending feature made the shop's account pages run a calculation that tried to divide by zero, so those pages failed.
still_at_risk: If monthly-spend-feature is switched on again, account page requests could fail again with the same division by zero.
symptom: Shoppers' account pages failed
causal_chain 1: Shoppers' account page requests failed, well above the usual low level of failures. (cites AL1; Gbac1, under "Log lines it read, one per message"; G5309, under "Log lines it read, one per message")
causal_chain 2: Account page requests raised ZeroDivisionError at src/io_shop/spend_summary.py:47. These errors were logged over {G5309.3} and were not seen in the log window before the onset. (cites G5309, under "Log lines it read, one per message"; G46bc, under "Log lines it read, one per message")
causal_chain 3: The spend-summary code ran because admin switched the feature flag monthly-spend-feature on at {P1.1}. Flag evaluations were split between off and on in {G971b.6} and were all on over {Gce95.4}. Before that, the flag was off over {G7e5d.4}. (cites P1, under "Changes to production it read"; G971b, under "Log lines it read, one per message"; Gce95, under "Log lines it read, one per message"; G7e5d, under "Log lines it read, one per message")
causal_chain 3 ruled_out 3: The ClientDisconnected account page errors: they were already logged before the onset, over {G46bc.3}, while account pages otherwise rendered normally. (cites G46bc, under "Log lines it read, one per message"; Gad41, under "Log lines it read, one per message")
causal_chain 4: The flag change broke account pages because the spend-summary path it turned on divides by a value that was zero on these requests. (cites G5309, under "Log lines it read, one per message")
contributing_factors 1: The flag change reached all account page traffic in a single step. No staged rollout and no automatic halt on a rising error rate were seen for monthly-spend-feature.
contributing_factors 1 had_it_been_otherwise: A small first share of traffic would have hit the division by zero, and the rollout could have stopped before most account page requests failed.
contributing_factors 2: No test or pre-production check of the spend-summary path was seen before the flag was switched on in production.
contributing_factors 2 had_it_been_otherwise: A check that ran the spend-summary path on account data like production's could have hit the ZeroDivisionError before any shopper did.
contributing_factors 3: The HighErrorRate alert on io-shop was not linked to on-call paging, so nobody was paged when it fired.
contributing_factors 3 had_it_been_otherwise: An on-call engineer would have been told directly when the alert fired, rather than depending on someone noticing the incident.
action_items 1: Fix the division at src/io_shop/spend_summary.py:47 so a zero divisor cannot fail the account page, and add a test for that case, before monthly-spend-feature is switched on again.
action_items 2: Roll out monthly-spend-feature, and flags like it, in percentage stages that stop automatically when the service's error rate rises.
action_items 3: Require that the code path behind a feature flag passes tests on production-like data in a pre-production environment before the flag can be switched on in production.
action_items 4: Route the HighErrorRate alert for io-shop to the on-call paging rotation.

Not to be judged:
  - Names in braces, such as {T5.1} or {duration}, are figures code writes in from the row they name. They are not judged.
  - Action items propose what to do; they make no claim about the record.
  - Whether something went well, went wrong or was lucky is a judgement. Only a fact it states is judged, and whether a went_wrong item is one its field excludes.

Judge every claim in the document, and answer by calling judge_claims.

tools.description: Submit every claim in the document, each either as supported or as flagged. Supported: the document's own words, quoted exactly, and the record's rows that support it. Flagged: the document's own words, quoted exactly, why, and the record's rows that contradict it (none where no row speaks to it at all). Empty lists say the document makes no claim to judge.

why.description: One sentence: what the record holds instead. Never empty.

tools.name: judge_claims
